note: Early DEE cohorts report GTF3C3 in severe epileptic encephalopathy cases, while generalized neurodevelopmental/GeneMatcher cohorts observe seizures in only ~50% of affected patients.

evidence.text: In a cohort of four patients from three unrelated families collected through GeneMatcher presenting with microcephaly, developmental delay, and intellectual disability, seizures were reported in only half of the individuals.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: The patients exhibited microcephaly, developmental delay, intellectual disability and distinctive dysmorphic facies that appear recognizable in very young children... Seizures were observed in half of the patients.

numbers.metric: patients with seizures in GeneMatcher cohort

evidence.text: GTF3C3 was identified as a candidate disease gene in a whole-exome sequencing study specifically ascertaining patients with early-onset epileptic encephalopathy and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

source.title: The role of recessive inheritance in early-onset epileptic encephalopathies: a combined whole-exome sequencing and copy number study
source.quote: We further support candidacy for neurodevelopmental disorders of four previously described genes (PIK3AP1, GTF3C3, UFC1, and WRAP53), three of which also followed a recessive inheritance pattern.
